I’ve been feeling this jig is too repetitive and boring to play, but I got in trance with it this afternoon. The version I picked up from Kevin Burke’s playing is:

Scatter The Mud, X:7

I’ve heard some lovely performances of this old jig set in E dorian from the likes of Mirella Murray and Fiachra O’Regan--the latter just last night here in Nashville. This setting comes pretty straight from the solo box playing of Charlie Piggot on his wonderful recording with Gerry Harrington “The New Road”. Note the alternate endings of the B part.

↳ Posted by billwolfe on December 23rd, 2016.

Gerard Trimble’s version

Does anybody like GT’s wonderful version, from his epic cittern album First Flight ?
It’s a cracker. He adds a 3rd part, which includes phrases in D minor, which really works. He must have written it himself. He’s like that.
Anyway, I’ll transcribe it on here some time.

↳ Posted by Fliúiteadóir on November 27th, 2019.

Scatter The Mud, X:10

This is transcribed from the truly cracking Gerald Trimble version. Definitely a huge fan of that first album of his, the second and third get a little hit or miss for me but First Flight is just great. The liner notes for the LP mention that the tune shows up in two different settings in O’Neil’s but doesn’t mention anything about composing the C part. I wouldn’t be surprised if he had written it though. Those C naturals really add a haunting vibe that I enjoy. On this recording the structure is AABBCCBBAABB.
